summary: Discovery POC scoping focused on integration planning. Customer is evaluating Redwood for a 6-week POC to validate latency and cost for an OpenAI-compatible integration that uses function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs. Main concerns: latency at 100ms p50 for short chat flows, burst throughput for 200 qps, data residency and KMS integration. Agreed next steps include benchmark runs, sharing SOW, and a follow-up demo on tool-calling and structured outputs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO, Orion), Liam O'Connor (ML Eng), Priya Shah (Product)

[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we got about 50 minutes, want to make sure we cover success criteria, sizing, and the integration plan.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Yep thanks Sophie, appreciate it. Quick intro from our side - I'm Maya, CTO, Liam is our ML lead and Priya product. We're evaluating vendors for a POC to validate latency/cost and structured outputs for our agent workflows.
[00:25] Sophie Chen: Great, quick run through from our side, Daniel will cover benchmarks and SDK details. we also have our OpenAI-compatible endpoints so you can switch with minimal changes.
[00:34] Daniel Ortiz: hi all, quick note, our endpoints support both Redwood SDK and OpenAI-compatible REST, plus function/tool calling patterns and structured JSON outputs via response schemas.
[00:45] Priya Shah: When you say function calling, is that exactly the OpenAI schema we've been using? we rely on that heavily for our action routing.
[00:53] Daniel Ortiz: it's very similar; we support the same parameter and function signature patterns, a couple naming quirks in our telemetry but you can use the same client code. there may be small differences in error shapes.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: for the POC our target is p50 latency around 100ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and sustained 200 qps for peak times, we also want to run blast tests up to 500 qps for 2 minutes. cost is secondary but important.
[01:26] Sophie Chen: good, that's concrete. success criteria recap: 1) p50 <=100ms for 128 token chat turns, 2) sustained 200 qps under 95th percentile SLO, 3) structured outputs >= 98% schema compliance on validation set, 4) documented integration + KMS for keys. does that look right?
[01:45] Maya Patel: yes that's right, and data residency - logs must remain in our region and we need KMS integration or HSM for encryption at rest.
[01:55] Daniel Ortiz: we support customer-managed KMS and VPC/private deployment for the POC if needed; for hosted POC we can enable per-tenant encryption and region pinning.
[02:10] Sophie Chen: timeline-wise we usually do a 4-6 week POC: week 0 onboarding, week 1 baseline benchmarks, week 2 integration + function calling test, week 3 run structured output evals, week 4 tuning and final report. we can compress if you have firm deadlines.
[02:28] Maya Patel: 6 weeks is fine but we want baseline data in two weeks.
[02:33] Daniel Ortiz: ok we'll prioritize that. On the tech side, for SDKs we support our python/js SDKs; example integration is basically swapping the client import and url key - so minimal code changes. we also have an Express example and serverless snippet.
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: do you provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints so we don't have to refactor our backend?
[02:56] Daniel Ortiz: yes, you can keep the same OpenAI client and point it at our endpoint. we do recommend switching to Redwood SDK for observability and cost controls but it's optional for POC.
[03:05] Priya Shah: structured outputs - how do you handle schema drift? we need to validate JSON output and reject/fallback when off-schema.
[03:12] Daniel Ortiz: we have a schema enforcement layer - you can provide a JSON schema and we return a 'structured' block; on mismatch we can fallback to a parse-fix pass or call a repair function. that repair can be configured as part of the pipeline.
[03:28] Sophie Chen: we'll show a demo of that in the follow-up - it's helpful for product teams.
[03:34] Maya Patel: about benchmarks - what exactly will you run and what telemetry do we get?
[03:39] Daniel Ortiz: we'll run three types: latency distribution on representative prompt set at target token lengths, throughput tests at target qps (sustained and burst), and structured-output fidelity checks against your validation set. we typically share raw logs, per-route p50/p90/p99, token cost estimates, and KV cache hit rates if applicable.
[03:57] Liam O'Connor: can you run tests against our staging environment or do you need us to send prompts?
[04:02] Daniel Ortiz: both work. easiest is you to provide a 1-week sample workload or provide a staging endpoint where we can run controlled load. we do not store payloads unless opted in.
[04:12] Maya Patel: ok we'll provide sample logs and a small staging key.
[04:16] Priya Shah: security review - we will need SOC2 docs, SAML SSO integration, and an audit of data flow.
[04:22] Sophie Chen: yep we will share our security pack and schedule a follow-up with security if needed.
[04:27] Maya Patel: anything else on model variants and quantization? we run a mix of/open models and some licensed models. cost wise we might use quantized variants.
[04:35] Daniel Ortiz: we support model pinning and quantization profiles; part of the POC we'll recommend quantization that meets your fidelity targets. our Optimize tool suggests profiles by workload.
[04:46] Liam O'Connor: great. what about function/tool calling reliability under burst? sometimes the tool call adds latency.
[04:52] Daniel Ortiz: we instrument tool calls and you can configure sync vs async. for critical paths we recommend async and a short circuit fallback to a simpler model. we can simulate this in the benchmark.
[05:04] Sophie Chen: quick recap - deliverables from Redwood: SOW + pricing, benchmark plan, demo materials for tool-calling + structured outputs, security docs. deliverables from Orion: sample workload + staging access, success criteria signoff.
[05:18] Maya Patel: sounds good. any blockers for starting in the next week?
[05:22] Daniel Ortiz: none on our side; primary constraint is access to sample prompts/logs and decision on hosted vs dedicated for the POC. hosted is fastest.
[05:32] Priya Shah: we'll start with hosted to move fast, but we need KMS and region pinning enabled.
[05:38] Sophie Chen: we can enable customer-managed KMS on hosted for the POC and pin region - I'll include that in the SOW.
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: one more question - how do you measure structured output schema compliance? what's the tooling?
[05:50] Daniel Ortiz: we run automated validators against provided JSON schema and report percent compliance. we also surface common failure modes and examples so you can iterate on prompts.
[06:02] Maya Patel: ok that's helpful.
[06:05] Sophie Chen: any other concerns?
[06:08] Maya Patel: not from my side.
[06:10] Priya Shah: no.
[06:12] Liam O'Connor: fine.
[06:15] Sophie Chen: great we'll send the SOW and schedule follow-up demo for tool-calling on Oct 22. thanks everyone.
[06:23] Maya Patel: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript: transcription contains some minor speaker mislabels and typical filler words; timestamps approximate every 10-60s.
